title: Beef, round, top round, boneless, choice, raw

content.title: About
content.content: Top round beef is a lean cut from the rear leg of cattle. This version is boneless, graded as Choice (second‑highest quality in the US), and sold raw. The meat has a deep red color, moderately tender texture, and a classic beef flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Top round is one of the leanest beef cuts, often used for roasting, grilling, and making deli‑style roast beef.
Because of its low fat content, it is popular in low‑calorie and high‑protein diets.
"Choice" indicates a high level of marbling and tenderness, just below the premium "Prime" grade.
Boneless top round is convenient for thin slicing, making it ideal for sandwiches and salads.
Raw beef should be stored at 0 °C–4 °C to limit bacterial growth.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: A 100‑g serving provides about 20 g of high‑quality protein, essential for muscle repair and growth.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Top round contains less than 5 g of fat per 100 g, making it suitable for low‑fat eating plans.

items.title: Provides iron and zinc
items.content: Beef is a good source of heme iron and zinc, which support immune function and oxygen transport.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains vitamin B12, niacin (B3) and riboflavin (B2), important for energy metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Creatine and carnosine
items.content: These compounds help improve muscular strength, endurance, and have antioxidant properties.

items.title: Bacterial contamination risk
items.content: Raw beef can harbor pathogens such as E. coli and Salmonella. Keep it refrigerated and cook to an internal temperature of at least 63 °C.

items.title: High purine content
items.content: People with gout should moderate intake of red meat, which can increase uric acid levels.

items.title: Meat allergy
items.content: Rare, but some individuals may experience allergic reactions to beef proteins.

items.title: Sodium in processed cuts
items.content: If the meat has been pre‑salted, consider total sodium intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Top round can be roasted, grilled, pan‑seared, or braised. For steaks, marinate briefly in olive oil, garlic, and herbs, then cook to the desired doneness. Thinly sliced pieces are perfect for sandwiches, salads, and stir‑fries.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep raw top round in its original packaging or an airtight container in the refrigerator at 0–4 °C for 3–5 days. For longer storage, freeze at –18 °C, where it retains quality for 6–12 months. Thaw frozen meat in the refrigerator, not at room temperature.
